question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool execution mode to the core agent loop, and must that wait for explicit tool concurrency-safety metadata before any early execution is allowed?
rationale: The source-level latency opportunity is clear, but the fix changes core runtime semantics and safety policy instead of repairing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open for an owner design covering early scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

options.title: Block On Safety Metadata
options.body: Treat this as dependent on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract before implementing early execution.

options.title: Defer Runtime Semantics Change
options.body: Leave current post-stream parallel batching as the only supported behavior if maintainers decide the safety and ordering tradeoffs are not worth the latency win right now.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for an owner design covering early scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent central agent-loop and provider-stream history points to this owner for the runtime scheduling decision.
